title: Signed-artifact fallback and satellite mirror scheduling for private deployments (partial egress approval flow)
creator: Maya Ortega
description: Define and validate an operational contract for private/VPC deployments that ensures robust bootstrap when full egress is disallowed. The contract covers: signed-artifact verification, a prioritized fallback to customer-controlled satellite mirrors, a predictable mirror sync schedule and backoff behavior, and an explicit partial-egress approval flow for short-lived egress windows. Deliverables include acceptance criteria, operator runbook changes, and an integration test harness for offline bootstrap + satellite mirror fallback scenarios.
background: Customers deploying Redwood Private in high-regulation environments frequently disallow outbound network access. Current bootstrap relies on a single canonical artifact host and assumes operator-level transient egress for image and artifact retrieval. We need a formalized fallback path so operators can bootstrap and upgrade clusters deterministically without manual artifact transfers or ad-hoc scripts. Existing specs cover broad airgap upgrade constraints but lack an explicit signed-artifact fallback sequence and scheduling for satellite mirrors used by internal NetOps teams.
goals: Define a signed-artifact verification contract compatible with on-prem KMS and image-signing key rotation
Specify a prioritized fallback sequence: canonical registry -> known satellite mirror(s) -> operator-provided offline bundle
Standardize a mirror sync schedule with jitter/backoff and measurable SLAs for artifact freshness
Design a partial-egress approval flow (timebound, auditable) for operators to request short-lived egress for edge cases
Produce acceptance criteria, test harness scenarios, and operator runbook changes
out_of_scope: Implementation of third-party satellite mirror software (we specify expectations and validation only)
Changes to public hosted API billing or pricing
New cryptographic algorithms beyond current signing primitives (we rely on existing RSA/ECDSA schemes)
scope: PRD-level artifact signature format and verification steps for the operator and bootstrap OLM
Operator-facing partial-egress request API and audit trail schema
Mirror prioritization rules and scheduling policy with retry/backoff semantics
Acceptance test harness for automated bootstrap in zero-egress, satellite-mirror-only, and offline-bundle-only modes
Runbook text for on-call and install-time operator guidance
acceptance_criteria: Bootstrap success in a zero-egress environment using a pre-seeded offline bundle (automated test)
Bootstrap success when canonical registry is unreachable but a prioritized satellite mirror is available (automated test)
All artifacts must validate against a signed manifest; test harness rejects unsigned or tampered artifacts
Mirror sync schedule validated: mirrors receive a signed manifest within configured window (default 4 hours) after upstream publish in 90% of trials
Partial-egress request flow allows an operator to request a single egress window (max 30 minutes) which is logged to audit and can be revoked; API responds with signed approval token
KMS rotation: operator can rotate a signing key and the bootstrap path recognizes and validates both current and previous keys for a configurable overlap window (default 48 hours)
Rollback criteria: if >5% of nodes report checksum mismatches during upgrade stage within 10 minutes, automated rollout pauses and can be safely rolled back by operator command
Performance: artifact verification adds <=300ms on average to install-time artifact fetch processing per artifact on typical on-prem control-plane hardware
Security: manifests and approvals include non-replayable timestamps and nonce; automated tests prove replay attempts are rejected
test_plan: Create automated scenarios in the CI harness that simulate: (1) zero-egress + offline bundle only, (2) canonical-down + satellite-mirror available, (3) canonical + satellite both available with mirror lag, (4) signing key rotation window, (5) partial-egress token issuance and revocation. Each scenario should assert success/failure per acceptance criteria and publish per-test artifacts to the internal test dashboard.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Spec review and security sign-off (2 weeks). Phase 2: Build verification hooks and CI scenarios (3 weeks). Phase 3: Operator runbook drafts and on-prem validation with two pilot customers (2 weeks). Phase 4: GA docs + console UI for partial-egress requests (1 week). Require a coordinated release with Private control-plane 2026.04 and operator SDK v0.9.
risks: Operators may misuse partial-egress to bypass airgap policies — mitigated by approval tokens, short TTLs, and audit logs
Satellite mirror staleness could cause silent failure — mitigated by freshness checks and manifest-based validation
Key rotation complexity introduces validation edge cases — mitigated by overlap window and early-warning alerts
open_questions: What is the minimum acceptable mirror freshness window for enterprise customers that operate daily change windows?
Should we support multiple signature algorithms in parallel for customers with legacy HSMs?
Who owns partial-egress approval: customer NetOps, Redwood-managed SRE, or joint? Need decision for UI and audit UX.
operator_runbook_notes: Include step-by-step for: pre-seed offline bundle generation, registering satellite mirror endpoints, requesting partial-egress token, validating signed manifest locally, and manual rollback triggers. Embed CLI examples and sample audit entries.
implementation_acceptance: Engineering must deliver a reproducible CI job per acceptance test and a small integration demo with one pilot customer. Security must perform a threat model and sign off on the partial-egress protocol before we mark Done.
notes: This spec intentionally separates artifact verification (cryptographic) from distribution topology (mirrors/offline bundles). Teams should avoid adding bilateral operator-only scripts; prefer deterministic, testable sequences.
